column2: Last week, site ten lost three hundred pounds a week. But money doesn't just disappear. Something on that street takes it. Five things, in fact.
Michael Porter called them the five forces. On an MBA, they judge a whole industry. Owners usually stop there. Run them on a single site instead, and each force becomes a line on its P and L.

Start with suppliers. Food is thirty percent of site ten's sales. The landlord takes twenty. And Porter counts labour as a supplier too: forty percent. Ninety pence in every pound is spoken for before a guest walks in.
Next, buyers. A guest can walk next door, so your prices have a ceiling. And delivery apps sit between you and that guest. On a twenty pound order, up to six pounds can go in commission.
Then substitutes: the meal deal, the office canteen, cooking at home. New entrants: the empty unit opposite is a rival in waiting. And existing rivals cut prices to win your guests.
So before you sign the next lease, score each street from one to five on every force. Street A scores twelve. Street B scores twenty-one. Street B needs more sales just to stand still.
Your question for Monday: which force takes the biggest cut at each of your sites?
